discharges.prior_disposition: deferred: cross-corpus independence beyond raw source bytes

overall_finding.statement: The ES and P-vs-NP corpora draw on disjoint primary subject-matter sources (zero shared citations, zero shared cited authors, code-verified SHA-256 disjointness) but share the corpus author, selection authority, annotation template, posture vocabulary, outcome-label source, decision rule, and execution path. Independent corpus construction is not established; independent subject matter under common construction is.

units_compared.note: Four ES databases share 12/13 source_snapshots.sha256 byte-for-byte per source-lineage-check-result.md: one corpus at four HEADs. n=2 corpus lineages, not 5.

evidence: Zero shared citations between corpora; disjoint cited-source sets.
ES cited anchors: Mordell 1969; Elsholtz & Tao 2011-2013; Browning & Elsholtz 2010-2011; Vaughan 1970; Monks & Velingker; arXiv:2404.01508.
pvnp cited anchors: Baker-Gill-Solovay 1975; Razborov-Rudich 1994/1997; Mulmuley-Sohoni 2001; Kabanets-Impagliazzo 2003; Hastad; Smolensky.
corpus/README.md: notes are 'project-authored summaries for normalization, not original mathematics and not verified proofs'.
corpus/experiments/pvnp-holdout/RESULT.md: corpus is 'not raw historical text'.
qualifications: ES has only 2 machine-resolvable identifiers (arXiv IDs) across 13 files; remaining sourcing is prose in an Era line that corpus/README.md declares 'not audited'.
pvnp corpus files contain zero arXiv/DOI/URL tokens; DOIs live in SCOPE.md and records/date-source-0{1,2}.json.
Neither corpus retains primary source bytes, so raw-source identity is verified against stated anchors only.
missing_evidence: Retained or hashed primary source bytes for either corpus.
A pvnp source register with per-source read_scope comparable to corpus/research/erdos-straus-2026-09-10/sources.json.
Record of which passages were actually consulted while authoring either corpus.

evidence: Cross-check of 49 author surnames across both corpora returns strict partition: no name appears in both.
No cross-citation in either direction; rg 'Erd|erdos|residue' over pvnp-holdout/train/*.md returns zero hits.
newf source lineage-diff verdict 'disjoint': left prb_01M2B8ZMHRCJN4YVH4CP6SNXTD (.newf/m7/newf.db, 12 snapshots) vs right prb_01M2BKVV5A7HD9HSAQKG7XEDST (.newf/pvnp/newf.db, 12 snapshots), shared 0.
Only ES mentions anywhere in the pvnp tree are two apparatus references in SCOPE.md, not source citations.
missing_evidence: Verification is against stated anchors, not against what was actually consulted.

evidence: All 27 corpus files declare schema_version 'normalize/v1'.
Payload key sets identical at top, approach, and outcome levels; pvnp mechanism level is the same 10 keys plus completeness_basis, completeness_scope, field_completeness (additive only).
pvnp-holdout/SCOPE.md:66: 'Each file follows the corpus/train/ shape: prose + newf-normalize payload with mechanism axes'.

Prompts near-identical across corpora: corpus/experiments/pilot-001/prompts/b0.md vs corpus/experiments/pvnp-holdout/captures/b0-prompt.md share headings, wire-schema paragraphs, and constraint list, with the domain sentence swapped.

provenance_gap.es_attribution: 'project-authored' only (corpus/README.md, README.md, pilot-001/PROTOCOL.md); no model, provider, version, or session.
provenance_gap.pvnp_attribution: 'Author-attested 2026-09-12 as part of pvnp-holdout corpus preparation', repeated verbatim in completeness_basis of all 14 files; no model, provider, version, or session.
provenance_gap.contrast: corpus/experiments/pilot-003/captures/config.json records proposer and model_identity for downstream capture steps, so the absence at corpus-authoring time is a provenance gap, not a repository convention.

missing_evidence: Model/provider/version/session identity for corpus authoring in both corpora.
Any authoring transcript or session capture for the notes themselves.
Whether the pvnp author had ES payloads in context while writing.

evidence: normalize/v1 defined once at internal/normalize/schema.go:20; used by all 27 files.
Same three posture axes with same code-validated enums at internal/domain/normalize.go:336-342 (locality, construction_mode, uncertainty_mode).

mechanism/v* vocabulary family seeded from one file internal/canon/vocabulary_seed.go; ES pins mechanism/v3 (m7-blinded-run/run.sh:20) and mechanism/v1 (pilot-001), pvnp pins mechanism/v6 declared as a v5 superset.
Shared comparison profile classify/v3 (internal/canon/compare.go:87) with profile sha 34b4bf219dcacebd7c58b1917723d525f19491918e705357c5c6fd63c6ec91b2 present in readiness records for both corpora.
missing_evidence: Nothing missing for this disposition; shared identifiers are exact. No corpus in the repository uses a schema or posture vocabulary not derived from internal/normalize plus internal/canon.

evidence: Outcome labels are author-supplied inside each note's own embedded payload (outcome.class with self-declared support array) on both sides; no independent labeller recorded for either corpus.
Shared decision rule recovery-rule/v1 (internal/experiment/recovery.go:23) recorded for ES (m7-blinded-run, pilot-003, pilot-001) and pvnp (pvnp-holdout/records/run.json, SCOPE.md).
Shared leakage checker leakage-check/v1 (internal/store/experiment_store.go:245) cited in both corpora's records.

Adjudication rubric is the same template with the domain criterion swapped: same 4-question passage-level structure, same three-verdict enum (recovers / does_not_recover / cannot_assess), same mandatory procedural-cue clause.
pvnp-holdout/RESULT.md:91-94 records the shared-model-family limitation explicitly; ES makes no equivalent statement.
missing_evidence: Independent (non-author, non-same-model-family) outcome labelling for either corpus.
ES adjudicator or model identity for corpus-level outcome labels.

evidence: Both corpora normalized with --provider fixture; single implementation internal/provider/fixture.go.
fixture.go derives mechanism axes by parsing the author's own embedded newf-normalize JSON (fixtureBlockStart '<!-- newf-normalize'), so the normalized representation was hand-authored in both cases.
Same verb chain: init, ingest, normalize --provider fixture, mechanism signature, cluster build, failure-space build, invariants mine --emit-posture-axes, challenge.
Same miner eligibility code path derivePostureAxisProposals applied across all five databases per l-population-validation-result.md.
asymmetries: ES has a committed reproducible runner corpus/experiments/m7-blinded-run/run.sh; pvnp has none.
.newf/ is gitignored, so the database artifacts backing the lineage evidence are not reproducible from a fresh clone.
missing_evidence: A committed reproducible runner for pvnp.
Any second independent implementation to cross-check normalization or mining.

most_consequential_finding: internal/provider/fixture.go derives each corpus's normalized mechanism axes by parsing the corpus author's own embedded newf-normalize JSON. For both corpora the representation the miner, challenger, and recovery rule operate on was hand-authored by the same author, in the same template, under the same vocabulary. Source-byte disjointness sits upstream of this and does not touch it.
claims_constrained: ES and pvnp are two independent research replications: not supported.
Agreement between the corpora corroborates a domain-general property: constrained, because shared annotator, template, vocabulary, and decision rule mean agreement can reflect the instrument.
Divergence between the corpora reflects a domain difference: constrained, because divergence could reflect the mechanism/v3 vs mechanism/v6 vocabulary difference or single-pass annotation choices.
The l-pvnp-replication partial-replication reading generalizes: already capped at PE; this audit supplies the reason the observation is not independent.
claims_unaffected: The source-byte disjoint verdict itself (SGO, retained).
Deterministic code-level results in the l-coh arc, including correction 5's CMA fixture test.
pvnp's internal chronology discipline and leakage audit.

what_would_establish_independence.corpus_selection: Inclusion/exclusion criteria authored by a party who did not author the notes, recorded before source screening.
what_would_establish_independence.annotation_construction: A different annotator with the authoring identity actually recorded.
what_would_establish_independence.representation: A schema or vocabulary not derived from internal/normalize plus internal/canon, or independent re-annotation under a second vocabulary.
what_would_establish_independence.outcome_assessment: Outcome labels supplied by a party other than the note author, without reference exposure.
what_would_establish_independence.execution: A second implementation cross-checking normalization and mining.
what_would_establish_independence.third_corpus_note: A third corpus discharges none of these for the existing pair. Adding a third corpus cannot retroactively make ES and pvnp independent of each other.
